content.prompt: Use set notation to describe the shaded sets.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 62, upper-left diagram in the 2 × 2 group
spec.description: Only the common lens of A and B is shaded; rectangle and exterior remain white. Labels have short leaders.
spec.mathematics: Two overlapping sets with the common region selected.
spec.answerVisibility: Shading is supplied question data; no symbolic answer is printed.

answer.worked: Only points belonging to both $A$ and $B$ are shaded, so the set is $A\cap B$.

spec.description: Both circles and their overlap are uniformly shaded; exterior white. Labels A left and B right with short leaders.
spec.mathematics: Two overlapping sets with both interiors selected.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied region shading only; no symbolic answer.

answer.worked: The shading includes every point in either circle, including their overlap. The set is $A\cup B$.

spec.description: Both exclusive crescents shaded; overlap and exterior white.
spec.mathematics: Membership in exactly one of A and B.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied region shading only; no symbolic answer.

answer.worked:
The left crescent is $A\cap\overline B$ and the right crescent is $B\cap\overline A$. Combine these two shaded regions:
$$(A\cap\overline B)\cup(B\cap\overline A).$$

spec.description: Entire rectangle shaded except the B-only crescent; A and the overlap remain shaded.
spec.mathematics: All regions except B outside A.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied region shading only; no symbolic answer.

answer.worked: All of $A$ is shaded, together with everything outside $B$. Only the $B$-only crescent is unshaded. The set is $A\cup\overline B$, with the rectangle as the universal set.
